- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) or shows strong downward momentum, model frequently underestimates drop; add 1–2% buffer to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Model exhibits persistent lag in downward corrections — if true price drops below 75% of recent high, forecast should adjust downward by 2–5% faster than historical pattern.
- For 30-day horizon, model overestimates early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is bullish; apply 1–3% downward adjustment to first 5 days.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model tends to average out; use sentiment-weighted smoothing: higher weight to recent sentiment if >0.50, lower if <0.40.
